title: LoRA Rank as a Control Variable for Emergent Misalignment Severity
original_idea: Fine-tune a small model on the insecure-code dataset using LoRA adapters at ranks 1, 4, 16, 64, and 128. Hold all other hyperparameters constant. Measure misalignment rate and coherence for each rank.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: LoRA rank affects EM severity -> if low rank = less misalignment, rank constraints as safety norm; if high rank = more, informs safe deployment. Each link is explicit. Directly actionable for practitioners choosing fine-tuning hyperparameters.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: A single hyperparameter sweep using existing codebase and datasets. Changing LoRA rank is a one-line configuration change. Uses standard tools (PEFT, TRL). A motivated beginner with basic Python can run five fine-tuning jobs following documentation.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: one hyperparameter sweep (five values), one model, one dataset, one evaluation set. Well-defined success criteria (misalignment rate vs rank curve). Single experiment, can go from start to result very quickly.

novelty.reasoning: While the interaction between LoRA fine-tuning and safety alignment has been studied (Safe Pruning LoRA, arXiv:2506.18931; LoRA safety degradation in general), the specific experiment of varying LoRA rank as a control variable for emergent misalignment severity has not been published. SPLoRA identifies safety-critical LoRA layers and proposes pruning, which is related but operates post-hoc rather than as a rank-sweep experiment. The finding that 'middle layers are more important for reasoning-safety trade-offs' is suggestive but does not directly characterize rank-EM curves. The observation that fine-tuning even with benign data can compromise safety alignment through LoRA is documented, but no systematic rank-vs-misalignment-rate curve has been published. This is a tractable, well-specified gap.

Safe Pruning LoRA (SPLoRA).details: Confirmed via arXiv:2506.18931. Identifies safety-critical LoRA layers using Empirical-DIEM metric. Related but addresses pruning rather than rank variation.

Fine-Tuning Lowers Safety.details: Confirmed via ACL LLMSec 2025. Documents safety degradation from fine-tuning but does not isolate LoRA rank as a variable.
